title: Supported Cartier Kummer map for ordinary etale arbitrary finite coefficients
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $N\geq1$ be invertible on $T$, and let $A$ be a finite commutative ring with $NA=0$. Let $i:D\hookrightarrow T$ be an effective Cartier divisor: its ideal is locally generated by one non-zero-divisor [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal], and let $j:T\setminus D\hookrightarrow T$ be its open complement. Use the ordinary small etale module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] and the twist $A_T(1)=\mu_{N,T}\otimes_{(\mathbf Z/N)_T}A_T$ of [lem-asd-finite-etale-twist-line]. The line bundle $\mathcal O_T(D)$ [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle] with its canonical trivialization off $D$ has a supported Kummer boundary for the exact sequence of [lem-amb-kummer-any-base]. This boundary determines a canonical morphism
$$c_{D,A}:Ri_*A_D\longrightarrow A_T(1)[2].$$
If $u_D:A_T\longrightarrow Ri_*A_D$ is the inverse-image/direct-image unit, then $c_{D,A}u_D=c_1(\mathcal O_T(D))$, where $c_1$ is the Kummer boundary followed by derived scalar extension from $\mathbf Z/N$ to $A$. For every morphism $v:T'\to T$ whose scheme-theoretic pullback $D'=T'\times_TD$ remains an effective Cartier divisor, the canonical closed-immersion exchange identifies $v^{-1}c_{D,A}$ with $c_{D',A}$. The map is the derived scalar extension of $c_{D,\mathbf Z/N}$, using the canonical identifications of its source and target with $Ri_*A_D$ and $A_T(1)[2]$.

source.place: Tag 03PL, lemma-kummer-sequence, applied to the relative line-bundle class; supported realization follows the relative-cone construction in the blueprint lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map.md, with ordinary roots-of-unity twist and derived scalar extension; Tag 0A45, lemma-cohomology-with-support-triangle (etale-cohomology.tex), and the supported-Hom interface of lem-amb-closed-support-hom

proof.text: Put $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/N$ and $V=T-D$. The dual ideal $L$ of [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle] has a canonical section $s_D$, dual to $\mathcal I_D\hookrightarrow\mathcal O_T$. On an open chart where $\mathcal I_D=(f_a)$ with $f_a$ a nonzerodivisor, the ideal is free on $f_a$, its dual is free on $e_a=f_a^{-1}$, and $s_D=f_ae_a$. On $V=T-D$, $f_a$ is a unit, so $s_D$ is a nowhere zero section and gives a specified trivialization $\tau_D:\mathcal O_V\cong L|_V$. On overlaps $e_b=(f_a/f_b)e_a$, hence these formulas agree. The frame torsor $P_D=\underline{\operatorname{Isom}}(\mathcal O_T,L)$ of [lem-sc-line-bundle-torsor] is therefore a $\mathbf G_m$-torsor with the specified section $\tau_D$ on $V$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 1: divisor section and trivialization

proof.text: Apply [lem-amb-relative-torsor-cohomology] to $(P_D,\tau_D)$ with $G=\mathbf G_m$. This gives a specified class $\alpha_D\in H^1(T,V;\mathbf G_m)$, independent of chart equations and refinements, whose forgotten-support image is the torsor class of $L$. For explicit changes of equations, $f'_a=u_af_a$ gives $e'_a=u_a^{-1}e_a$ and $f'_ae'_a=f_ae_a$; it is the same line bundle with the same section, not just an unspecified lift of its Picard class. The relative lemma supplies the comparison with derived sections; no assertion that an arbitrary ordinary Cech cover computes all derived cohomology is needed.

Since $N$ is invertible on $T$, [lem-amb-kummer-any-base] supplies the short exact Kummer sequence $0\to\mu_N\to\mathbf G_m\xrightarrow{N}\mathbf G_m\to0$. Apply its relative connecting map, provided by [lem-amb-relative-torsor-cohomology], to $\alpha_D$: $\beta_D=\delta_{T,V}(\alpha_D)\in H^2(T,V;\mu_N)$. The relative lemma's compatibility with forgetting support gives $\operatorname{forget}(\beta_D)=\delta_T([L])$, exactly $c_{1,\Lambda}(L)$. Only the abelian-sheaf Kummer sequence is used: $\mathbf G_m$ is not a $\Lambda$-module and is never tensored over $\Lambda$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 3: Kummer boundary; Stacks Tag 03PL, lemma-kummer-sequence

proof.text: Use the canonical comparisons from module-derived sections to abelian-derived sections for the sheaf $\mu_N$ on $T$ and its restriction on $V$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-module-cohomology-forget] they induce isomorphisms on every cohomology group, hence are quasi-isomorphisms. They commute with restriction because both restriction maps send a section to its restriction. Taking their cones therefore identifies $H^2(T,V;\mu_N)$ with the relative cohomology computed in $\Lambda$-module sheaves; the projection from the shifted cone to the $T$-sections complex also commutes with these comparisons. Taking degree two in [lem-amb-closed-support-hom], with coefficient ring $\Lambda$ and $K=\mu_N[0]$, identifies it with $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(T_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)}(i_*\Lambda_D,\mu_{N,T}[2])$. Define $c_{D,\Lambda}$ to be the morphism corresponding to $\beta_D$. The forget-support map is precomposition with $\Lambda_T\to i_*\Lambda_D$: applying derived Hom to this map is the first arrow into the ordinary sections complex in the support cone. Thus step 3 is precisely the required first Chern class assertion. This is a support-Hom identification and uses no purity isomorphism. The forget-support compatibility can be checked directly using [lem-weil-pbc-open-closed-short-exact] for $F=\Lambda_T$. Apply derived Hom into $\mu_N$ to $j_!\Lambda_V\to\Lambda_T\to i_*\Lambda_D$. [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction] identifies Hom out of $j_!\Lambda_V$ with sections on $V$, and the counit induces restriction. Thus the relative fibre projects to sections on $T$ by precomposition with the displayed unit. This fixes the maps, not just an abstract isomorphism of cohomology groups.

source.place: Proof paragraphs 3-4: support-Hom; Stacks Tag 0A45, lemma-cohomology-with-support-triangle

proof.text: The closed immersion $i$ is finite because locally it is induced by a quotient ring. Therefore [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-direct-image-exact] gives exactness of $i_*$ on abelian sheaves. The module kernels and sheafified cokernels of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] have these underlying abelian kernels and cokernels, so $i_*$ is exact on module sheaves too. This identifies $Ri_*$ with $i_*$ on degree-zero objects. The derived scalar-extension comparison [lem-asd-supported-kummer-scalar-source] identifies $i_*\Lambda_D\otimes^L_\Lambda A$ with $i_*A_D$ and carries the constant unit to $u_D:A_T\to i_*A_D$.

source.place: Proof last paragraph: derived scalar extension; Stacks Tag 07A4, lemma-pullback-tensor-product

proof.text: Apply the triangulated change-of-rings functor [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. With $A=\Lambda$, [lem-asd-finite-etale-twist-line] says that $\mu_{N,T}$ is flat over $\Lambda_T$. Its degree-zero complex is K-flat: tensoring an acyclic complex with this exact tensor functor preserves kernels and images, so the resulting cohomology is zero in every degree. The K-flat computation therefore identifies the target $(\mu_{N,T}\otimes^L_\Lambda A_T)[2]$ with the ordinary tensor $A_T(1)[2]$.

source.place: Proof last paragraph: derived scalar extension; Stacks Tag 07A4, lemma-pullback-tensor-product

proof.text: Extending $c_{D,\Lambda}$ through these canonical source and target identifications defines $c_{D,A}$. The unit comparison of step 5 transports the equality $c_{D,\Lambda}u_D=c_1(\mathcal O_T(D))$ to $c_{D,A}u_D=c_1(\mathcal O_T(D))$ and proves the stated scalar-extension clause. No flatness of $A$ over $\Lambda$ is used. Here the transport is functoriality of the exact triangulated functor $-\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\Lambda_T}A_T$ of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]: it carries the composite $c_{D,\Lambda}\circ u_{D,\Lambda}$ to the composite of the extended maps, and the identification $\Lambda_T\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\Lambda_T}A_T=A_T$ (the degree-zero complex $\Lambda_T$ is K-flat over itself) is the one used in the definition of $c_1$.

source.place: Proof last paragraph: derived scalar extension; Stacks Tag 07A4, lemma-pullback-tensor-product

proof.text: Let $h:T'\to T$ and assume $D'$ is Cartier. The Cartier pullback lemma [lem-asd-supported-kummer-cartier-pullback] identifies $(h^*L,h^*s_D)$ with $(\mathcal O_{T'}(D'),s_{D'})$, including their complement trivializations. Pulling local equations back gives the same transition units; no flatness of $h$ is required.

source.place: Proof penultimate paragraph: Cartier-preserving base change

proof.text: Naturality of the relative torsor class and its Kummer connecting map in [lem-amb-relative-torsor-cohomology] sends $\alpha_D,\beta_D$ to $\alpha_{D'},\beta_{D'}$. The coefficient map $h^{-1}\mathbf G_m\to\mathbf G_m$ sends units and their $N$th powers to their pullbacks, so the Kummer sequence comparison commutes. The image of $(P_D,\tau_D)$ under the pullback of [lem-amb-relative-torsor-cohomology] followed by $h^{-1}\mathbf G_m\to\mathbf G_m$ is the frame torsor of $h^*L$ with the section $h^*\tau_D$: a local frame $e:\mathcal O_U\cong L|_U$ pulls back to the frame $h^*e$, equivariantly for the coefficient map, so the contracted product maps isomorphically to $\underline{\operatorname{Isom}}(\mathcal O_{T'},h^*L)$; by step 8 this pair is $(P_{D'},\tau_{D'})$. Finally the module-to-abelian comparisons of step 4 commute with these pullbacks: the pullback on derived sections is $R\Gamma(T,K)\to R\Gamma(T,Rh_*h^{-1}K)=R\Gamma(T',h^{-1}K)$ induced by the adjunction unit, forgetting coefficients commutes with $h^{-1}$ by the natural isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-module-pullback-forget-naturality], and with $Rh_*$ by the unit-compatible isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-module-abelian-derived-direct-image-comparison], on $T$ and on $V$ compatibly with restriction. Hence the module relative classes defining $c_{D,\Lambda}$ and $c_{D',\Lambda}$ correspond under pullback as the abelian ones do.

source.place: Proof penultimate paragraph: Cartier-preserving base change

proof.text: Apply [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] with coefficient ring $\Lambda$ to identify the canonical map $h^{-1}\mu_{N,T}\to\mu_{N,T'}$ with an isomorphism induced by pullback of roots, and with coefficient ring $A$ to identify the twists. The support-Hom naturality lemma [lem-asd-supported-kummer-support-hom-naturality] supplies the canonical invertible closed-constant exchange, so the supported sources are identified as well.

source.place: Proof penultimate paragraph: Cartier-preserving base change

proof.text: Apply the naturality of the supported-Hom identification [lem-asd-supported-kummer-support-hom-naturality] to the equality of the relative classes. Exact inverse image [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], monoidality [lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal], and pullback of constants [lem-kun-pullback-constant] transport the scalar-extension comparison. Substitution into the definition of $c_{D,A}$ gives $h^{-1}c_{D,A}=c_{D',A}$, including equality after forgetting support.

source.place: Proof penultimate paragraph: Cartier-preserving base change

proof.text: The auxiliary unique-boundary declaration in this module is proved by applying the separately proved normalized-boundary existence and uniqueness theorem [lem-asd-cartier-boundary-existence]. This does not discharge the remaining Chern, pullback, scalar and derived-arrow witnesses of the main theorem.
